items.description: Secs. 2.1 and 3.1 only say 'cantilever beam (Fig. 1(a))' and that the data came from top88. Which edge is fixed, and how much of it, appears only in Fig. 1(a). Unmodified top88 solves the half-MBB beam, so the authors must have changed the boundary conditions, but the text does not describe those changes.
readings: Entire left edge fixed (x = 0, 0 ≤ y ≤ H, all 101 nodes), as in top88's own cantilever variant (fixeddofs = 1:2*(nely+1))
Only part of the left edge fixed, e.g. the central half 0.25H ≤ y ≤ 0.75H
Entire right edge fixed with the load on the left edge (mirror image, same compliance)

items.description: 'Cantilever' suggests a clamped end, but the text never says which degrees of freedom are restrained. Only the support symbols in Fig. 1(a) show this.
readings: Fully clamped: ux = uy = 0 at every node on the support edge
Roller wall: ux = 0 along the edge, with uy fixed at a single node
Pins at discrete nodes only (e.g. the two corner nodes of the support edge)

items.description: The text (Secs. 2.1, 2.3, 3.1) gives no load location. It appears only in Fig. 1(a), and indirectly in the design images of Fig. 3(b) and Table 1.
readings: Bottom corner of the free (right) edge, (x, y) = (L, 0), as in the classic top99/top88 cantilever variant
Mid-height of the free edge, (L, 0.5H)
Top corner of the free edge, (L, H)

items.description: The text never gives the load direction; only Fig. 1(a) shows it. Reversing the sign does not change a single-load minimum-compliance design, but a load that is not transverse would.
readings: Vertical downward (−y), the usual cantilever tip load
Vertical upward (+y), giving the same layout and compliance
Inclined or horizontal, if Fig. 1(a) draws it that way

items.description: The text does not say whether the load is a single nodal force or spread over several nodes or an edge segment. Fig. 1(a) is the only source.
readings: Single nodal point force (top88 style)
Force spread over a few nodes or a short patch around the load point
Uniform traction over the whole free edge

items.description: No load magnitude is given anywhere in the text. top88 uses a unit force by default.
readings: F = 1 (top88 default)
A dimensional value, e.g. F = 1 kN

items.entity: Volume constraint for the cantilever run
items.description: The example is a sweep. Sec. 2.3 varies Vf from 0.01 to 0.95 in steps of 0.01, and also says a narrower range may be used if generation is hard. Table 1 shows Vf = 0.03, 0.25, 0.50 and 0.75, and Fig. 3(b) shows a target at an unstated Vf. No single value defines the example, and it is unclear which values were actually generated.
readings: Full sweep 0.01:0.01:0.95 (or a narrower subrange)

items.description: No material data are given for the cantilever (Secs. 2.1, 2.3). top88 uses E0 = 1 by default.
readings: E0 = 1 (top88 default, nondimensional)
A physical value, e.g. E0 = 210 GPa

items.description: Poisson's ratio is not stated anywhere; the top88 default is 0.3.
readings: nu = 0.3 (top88 default)

items.description: Sec. 2.3 gives only penal = 3. Neither the stiffness lower bound nor the SIMP form is stated (top88 uses E = Emin + x^p (E0 − Emin) with Emin = 1e-9). This matters most at very low Vf such as 0.03 in Table 1.
readings: Modified SIMP with Emin = 1e-9·E0 (top88)
Classic SIMP E = x^p·E0 with density lower bound xmin = 1e-3
Modified SIMP with Emin = 1e-6·E0

items.entity: Filter type flag ft = 1 and filter-radius definition
items.description: Sec. 2.3 gives the top88 inputs {penal=3, rmin=2.4, ft=1} as code flags but does not say what ft = 1 means or what units rmin uses. In top88, ft = 1 is sensitivity filtering with linear cone weights and rmin measured in element widths.
readings: Sensitivity filter, cone weights, rmin = 2.4 element widths (top88 ft = 1)
Density filter with rmin = 2.4 element widths

items.entity: Optimizer, initial design and stopping rule for the top88 runs
items.description: Sec. 2.3 lists maxit = 100 only for TOPress. For the top88 cantilever runs, the text gives no optimizer, move limit, initial design, convergence tolerance or iteration cap. The top88 defaults are OC, move limit 0.2, x0 = Vf, stop when the maximum change is ≤ 0.01, and no cap. Low-Vf runs (0.01–0.03) depend strongly on these choices.
readings: top88 defaults: OC (move 0.2, damping 0.5), uniform x0 = Vf, stop when max|Δx| ≤ 0.01, no iteration cap
Same as top88 defaults but capped at 100 iterations, as for TOPress
MMA with a comparable tolerance

items.entity: Physical size and thickness of the 100×100 domain
items.description: Sec. 2.3 and Sec. 4 fix a 100×100-element domain, so with square elements the domain is square (1:1). Physical dimensions, element size and out-of-plane thickness are not given. top88 assumes unit-size elements and unit thickness, with rmin in element units.
readings: 100 × 100 units, unit element size, unit thickness (top88 convention)
Unit square 1 × 1 with element size 0.01 and rmin scaled to 0.024
A dimensional size, e.g. 100 mm × 100 mm, with a chosen thickness

items.description: The text does not say whether the analysis is plane stress or plane strain, and it does not give the element formulation. top88 uses 4-node bilinear plane-stress quadrilaterals.
readings: Plane stress with bilinear Q4 elements (top88)
Plane strain with bilinear Q4 elements

items.description: The text mentions no passive solid or void regions for the cantilever, and Fig. 1(a) cannot be checked. top88 has none by default, so 'none' is the most likely reading.
readings: None: all 100×100 elements are designable
A small passive solid pad at the load point and/or along the support
